notes:
=== SharpChrome — Decrypt Chrome Saved Passwords ===
Extract AES key from Chrome's Local State file and decrypt Login Data SQLite database.

=== HOW CHROME ENCRYPTS PASSWORDS ===
Chrome stores saved passwords in: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data (SQLite)
Password column is encrypted with AES-256-GCM
AES key is stored in: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Local State (JSON file)
The AES key itself is encrypted with DPAPI (user's Windows login credentials)
SharpChrome decrypts the DPAPI-wrapped AES key, then decrypts all passwords

=== USAGE ===
  .\SharpChrome.exe logins   → decrypts and displays all saved passwords
  .\SharpChrome.exe cookies  → decrypts session cookies (Slack d cookie, etc.)
  .\SharpChrome.exe logins /target:C:\Users\<user>\   → target specific user profile

=== WHAT'S TYPICALLY FOUND ===
Internal web application credentials (SharePoint, Jira, Confluence)
Cloud platform credentials (AWS console, Azure portal, GCP)
VPN web portals and 2FA enrollment pages
External SaaS tools (Salesforce, GitHub, GitLab)
Email webmail interfaces

=== FORENSIC NOTE ===
Generates Event IDs: 4688 (process creation) and 16385 (DPAPI activity)
Defenders monitoring DPAPI events will detect this — minimize time between run and exfil
Only decryptable in context of owning user (DPAPI requires the user's credentials)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
SharpChrome → AWS console credentials → cloud pivot → IAM escalation → org-wide compromise
SharpChrome → GitHub credentials → source code → API keys embedded in code → further escalation
SharpChrome → corporate SSO credentials → access to all SSO-connected applications
After local admin escalation → access other users' Chrome profiles from their AppData

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Run on any user account with a Chrome profile → almost always has saved passwords
IT admin browser = highest value (has credentials for many systems)
Run after DPAPI key extraction from LSASS → can decrypt any user's Chrome data offline
SharpChrome cookies → extract Slack "d" cookie → hijack Slack session → internal comms

recommended.note: Steal session cookies from the same browser.

name: Credential Hunting - Chrome Saved Logins
description: SharpChrome (SharpDPAPI) decrypts saved Chrome logins using the current user's DPAPI keys, yielding plaintext site passwords.

defense.why_it_works: Chrome stores saved login credentials encrypted with DPAPI in the Login Data SQLite database. SharpChrome uses the same DPAPI decryption path that Chrome uses, recovering plaintext usernames and passwords for all saved sites. This works without cracking because the attacker is running as the user whose DPAPI master key protects the data.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as the target user (DPAPI master key accessible). Chrome must not have the database locked by a running Chrome instance, or a copy must be used. SharpChrome binary available.
defense.impact: Recovery of all usernames and passwords saved in Chrome for every website the user visits. May include VPN portals, corporate applications, and personal accounts that share credentials with corporate systems.
defense.detection: SharpChrome.exe execution (AV-detected). Access to Chrome Login Data SQLite database by non-Chrome process. Process: SharpChrome accessing %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data.
defense.artifacts: Process log: SharpChrome.exe executed | File access: Chrome Login Data read by non-Chrome process | EDR: credential harvesting from browser credential store
defense.prevention: Enable Chrome sync with account passwords (so stolen local credentials still require cloud authentication). Deploy endpoint protection detecting SharpChrome execution. Enforce MFA on all services so saved passwords require a second factor. Consider Google Advanced Protection Program for high-risk users.
defense.misconfiguration: No MFA enforced on corporate services — saved Chrome passwords provide direct access. No endpoint protection blocking SharpChrome. Chrome login database readable by non-Chrome processes without additional OS protection.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# SharpChrome retrieves all saved Chrome passwords:
.\SharpChrome.exe logins /unprotect
# Output: URL, username, password for all saved sites
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce MFA on all corporate services
# Even if passwords are stolen, MFA prevents access

# Google Chrome Enterprise: disable local password saving
# GPO: PasswordManagerEnabled = 0

# Use enterprise credential manager (Keeper, 1Password) instead of browser

# Monitor Chrome Login Data access by non-browser processes
